```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 110)
library(sciparseR)
```

The rules engine is precise but narrow. A language model reads more
varied writing, but it can also produce values that are not in the
paper. sciparseR uses language models in a way that keeps the second
problem visible: the model must quote its source, and the quote is
checked against the document before a value is accepted: the quote must
be in the cited passage (or be a cell of the cited table), a number must
appear in the quote as a whole number, a category must be stated there,
and arm, outcome and time point must appear in the passage. An answer
that is not valid JSON skips its chunk with a warning and is logged in
`x$llm$calls$error`; the other chunks are kept.

Nothing is sent anywhere unless you create an engine and pass it to
`sc_extract()`. Only block text and table cells are sent, never the PDF
file.

## Providers

sciparseR works with every provider of
[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org) and with ChatGPT plans through
[ellmercodex](https://github.com/simxnherrera/ellmercodex).

```{r}
sc_llm_providers()
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# API keys are read by ellmer from environment variables
eng <- sc_llm_engine("anthropic", model = "claude-sonnet-5-5")       # ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
eng <- sc_llm_engine("openai", model = "gpt-6")                       # OPENAI_API_KEY
eng <- sc_llm_engine("openrouter", model = "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5") # OPENROUTER_API_KEY
eng <- sc_llm_engine("google_gemini", model = "gemini-3-pro")         # GEMINI_API_KEY
eng <- sc_llm_engine("ollama", model = "llama4")                      # local, no key
eng <- sc_llm_engine("azure_openai", endpoint = "https://...", model = "my-deployment")
eng <- sc_llm_engine("aws_bedrock", model = "anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5")
```

Arguments after `model` go to the ellmer constructor (`credentials`,
`base_url`, `params`, and so on). Aliases `"claude"`, `"gemini"`,
`"bedrock"`, `"azure"` and `"vertex"` are accepted.

### ChatGPT plan

With an eligible ChatGPT plan, ellmercodex signs you in once and needs no
API key:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ellmercodex::codex_login()
eng <- sc_llm_engine("chatgpt", model = "gpt-6-luna", effort = "low")
```

Plan usage does not accept sampling arguments such as `temperature`.

### Your own chat or function

```{r, eval = FALSE}
chat <- ellmer::chat_openai_compatible(base_url = "http://localhost:8000/v1", model = "my-model")
eng <- sc_llm_engine(chat = chat)
```

A plain function also works. It receives the full prompt and returns JSON
or a data frame, which is how local inference servers, caching layers and
tests plug in.

## A complete run without network access

Here a function stands in for the model so the example runs anywhere. It
returns four answers: one correct, one with a value that is not in its
quote, one citing a block that was never sent, and one correct design
statement.

```{r}
doc <- sc_parse(system.file("extdata", "trial_tables.pdf", package = "sciparseR"))
b <- sc_blocks(doc, type = "paragraph")
bid <- b$block_id[grepl("total of 238", b$text)]

fake_model <- function(prompt) {
  jsonlite::toJSON(data.frame(
    field    = c("randomized_n", "analyzed_n", "comparator", "study_design"),
    value    = c("238", "236", "sham", "randomized_controlled_trial"),
    quote    = c("A total of 238 patients were randomly assigned",
                 "A total of 238 patients", "sham procedure",
                 "double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial"),
    block_id = c(bid, bid, "b-p009-0001", bid)))
}
eng <- sc_llm_engine(fun = fake_model, model = "stand-in")
eng
y <- sc_extract(doc, "clinical_trial", engine = "llm", llm = eng)
y$records[, c("field", "value", "status", "data_origin", "notes")]
```

* "238" and the design are quoted and present in the block: `reported`.
* "236" does not occur in its quote: `unsupported`.
* The "sham" quote cites a block that was not sent: `unsupported`.
* Required fields the model did not return are `not_reported`. When a
  model answer could not be read, part of the text was never assessed, so
  such fields are `not_assessed` instead and go to the review queue.
* A number must play a role in its quote that fits the field: the 95 of
  "95% CI" is an interval level, never an estimate or a sample size. A
  table value must sit in the row and column the model named, and the
  measure, interval level, unit, population and adjustment it attached
  must agree with the passage; otherwise the value is `unsupported` or
  `ambiguous`.
* Every model value has `data_origin = "model_inferred"`.

The evidence of verified values has offsets into the block text, so they
can be highlighted like rule based values:

```{r}
sc_evidence(y)[y$records$status == "reported", c("field", "value", "char_start", "char_end", "bbox_scope")]
```

## What the model sees

The prompt lists the schema fields with descriptions and allowed values,
then the passages, each prefixed with its block id. The system prompt
tells the model to quote exactly and not to compute or infer values.
Long documents are split into requests of at most `max_chars`
characters.

```{r}
cat(substr(sciparseR:::llm_prompt(sc_schema("pico"), b[1:2, ]), 1, 700))
```

## Run record

Each request is logged with the SHA-256 of its prompt, the number of
passages, the time taken and, for ellmer chats, tokens and cost:

```{r}
y$llm$calls
y$llm$model
```

## Structured output

ellmer structured output is used when the provider supports it. With the
default `structured = "auto"`, a provider that rejects it is asked for
plain JSON instead; `"always"` turns that fallback off and `"never"`
always uses plain JSON.

## Combining engines

A practical pattern is to run the rules engine first, then the model on
the same schema, and review where they disagree. Both results are
ordinary `sc_extraction` objects with the same columns.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
rules <- sc_validate(sc_extract(doc, "pico"))
model <- sc_validate(sc_extract(doc, "pico", engine = "llm", llm = eng))
merge(rules$records[, c("field", "value")], model$records[, c("field", "value")],
      by = "field", suffixes = c("_rules", "_model"))
```
